chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a garment and did not stipulate any condition with its seller. Then he disliked it and returned it to the seller, but the seller refused to accept it back except for a small deduction (price reduction). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to take it back with a deduction. If he was ignorant (of the ruling) and took it back and sold it for more than its price, he must return to the original seller whatever was the increase.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer returns an item without prior agreement on return conditions?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'fair compensation' in informal returns, ensuring the seller is not unjustly enriched by the buyer's unilateral deduction. It establishes that any profit derived from reselling the returned item must be returned to the original owner, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preventing *ghabn* (unfair loss) and maintaining equity in commercial transactions.
